site_name: Amazon Web Services Canton campus, Madison County Mega Site (Nissan Parkway and Highway 22)
notes: Utility: Mississippi Today (June 9, 2026, read via the OurTupelo republication because mississippitoday.org refused automated access) calls Entergy Mississippi 'Amazon's power provider' and quotes an Amazon spokesperson that Amazon 'currently has five buildings operational at the Canton site, with plans to at least double that presence.' Mississippi Free Press (2026, https://www.mississippifreepress.org/entergy-says-amazon-data-centers-will-help-mississippians-save-on-power-some-experts-fear-otherwise/) says Amazon's four campuses in Hinds, Madison and Warren counties are 'relying on Entergy to meet their power needs' and that the Entergy-Amazon contract is a trade secret under 2024 Senate Bill 2001 whose negotiated terms the Public Service Commission cannot modify, hence special_contract. Yazoo Valley EPA (the other mapped candidate) is not named in any source found. Energized year is NOT confirmed: 2025 rests only on a January 2024 Clarion Ledger report that Phase 1 at the Madison Megasite was 'expected to come online in January 2025' (a projection), plus the fact that the site was operating by mid-2026; groundbreaking was May 20, 2024 per Entergy. Treat 2025 as low confidence. No public megawatt figure for operating load was found (Entergy's CEO declined to state the load), so load_mw_2025 and full buildout are null; our 375.5 MW is unverified.

site_name: Amazon Web Services Ridgeland campus (Madison County, MS)
notes: Utility: Mississippi Free Press (2026) says Amazon's four Mississippi campuses (Hinds, Madison, Warren counties) are 'relying on Entergy to meet their power needs' and describes the April 9, 2026 announcement of an addition to the AWS campus in Ridgeland with Entergy Mississippi's CEO present; Mississippi Today (June 9, 2026, via https://ourtupelo.com/where-do-amazons-data-centers-in-mississippi-stand-company-offers-details-on-project-status-water-and-energy-footprint/) calls Entergy Mississippi 'Amazon's power provider.' Contract is a trade-secret agreement under 2024 Senate Bill 2001, hence special_contract. Energized year left null because sources conflict: a January 2024 Clarion Ledger report (https://www.yahoo.com/news/ms-power-grid-handle-amazon-172145562.html) projected Phase 2 at Ridgeland online in January 2026; Mississippi Free Press (April 2026) says Amazon 'already has an artificial intelligence data processing center in Ridgeland'; but an Amazon spokesperson told Mississippi Today in June 2026 that 'the Ridgeland site is in the early stages of construction.' Nothing found supports operation during 2025, so our 2026 is plausible but unconfirmed and a 2025 load of 228 MW is not supported. No public megawatt figure found for current load or full buildout.

site_name: NTT Global Data Centers Dallas campus TX1/TX2/TX3 (2008 Lookout Drive, Garland)
load_basis: Built critical IT load of TX1 only, per NTT's own TX1 page and Data Center Frontier (Dec 2023). TX2 and TX3 (about 36 MW each) were tenant fit-outs 'in development' in Dec 2023; whether they were energized by 2025 was not confirmed, so they are excluded.
notes: Utility: Data Center Knowledge (April 20, 2017), quoting the operator's release: RagingWire (now NTT) 'is working directly with Garland Power & Light to build a massive 108 MVA substation' next to TX1, with GP&L 'providing two new 138KV lines.' Ordinary municipal-utility service with a dedicated substation; no special contract found, so retail. First-phase grand opening was April 2017 (same article); Data Center Frontier (Dec 8, 2023, https://www.datacenterfrontier.com/site-selection/article/33016119/dcf-tours-ntt-global-data-centers-americas-dallas-tx1-garland-texas) says TX1 was 'made operational in 2017' and that the campus 'will provide 144 MW of critical IT load at full build-out' (the 2017 plan was 80 MW). Our energized year of 2024 (from a 2023 generator permit) is seven years late for the first building. Our 159.9 MW load looks like permitted generator capacity for the full campus, not 2025 load: confirmed built IT capacity is 16 MW, and at most about 88 MW if both 36 MW fit-outs finished, which was not verified. A fourth building was permitted with construction through April 2026 (Bisnow, April 30, 2024).

site_name: Google Midlothian data center campus (3441 Railport Pkwy)
notes: Serving utility NOT established. Four searches and several direct fetches (Dallas Morning News/NBC DFW 2019 and 2024, Bisnow Dec 2025, Midlothian Economic Development home page) found no source naming the delivery utility; none mentions United Cooperative Services (our fallback guess), Hilco Electric Cooperative, Navarro County EC or Oncor in connection with this site. Our guess was a flagged fallback and should be treated as unverified. Energized year also not found: NBC DFW/Dallas Morning News (June 14, 2019, https://www.nbcdfw.com/local/dfw-morningnews-googles-massive-600m-data-center-takes-shape-in-ellis-county-as-tech-giant-ups-texas-presence/215275/) says the project was 'under construction' with 'a lot of steel coming out of the ground', so first operation was after mid-2019 and our 2019 is probably a year or more early. No acceptable source gives a megawatt figure. Leads for a follow-up: City of Midlothian council records and the 2018 tax-abatement agreement with Sharka LLC; Public Utility Commission of Texas substation or certificate filings. A fifth building (288,000 sq ft, about $880M) was filed in December 2025 with completion in early 2027 (Bisnow).

site_name: CloudHQ LC campus, LC1A/LC1B/LC2/LC3 (21955 Loudoun County Parkway, Ashburn)
serving_utility: Virginia Electric & Power Co (Dominion Energy Virginia)
notes: Utility is an inference, not a finding: Dominion is the only mapped territory at this point and Loudoun County's data-center energy page refers to 'our regulated electric utility, Dominion', but no source found names Dominion as CloudHQ's provider or ties a specific substation to this campus (NOVEC also serves data centers in parts of Loudoun, so the county statement is not site-specific). Two searches of commission and Dominion project pages found no customer-specific filing. Energized year not found in any acceptable source (only directory sites give 2019-2020 for LC1), so null. No acceptable per-building megawatt figure for 2025. planned_full_buildout_mw is CloudHQ's own figure for the WHOLE LC campus ('1,256 MW Total Critical IT Load', 756 MW available, fourteen data centers; https://cloudhq.com/campus/lc-campus/), which also covers the separate worklist item at 22210 Loudoun County Parkway; do not sum it across the two items.

site_name: Yahoo Lockport data center (5319 Enterprise Dr, Lockport)
serving_utility: New York State Electric & Gas Corp (delivery); New York Power Authority hydropower allocation (supply)
load_basis: Sum of New York Power Authority hydropower allocations to the Lockport campus (15 MW at the outset, 1 MW added April 2011, 7.2 MW with the 2013-2015 expansion). This is contracted allocation, not metered load or stated IT capacity; no public load figure was found.
notes: Supply is low-cost hydropower allocated by contract from the New York Power Authority (10 MW for Phase I plus 5 MW for Phase II per the 2010 New York Senate release; one more MW approved April 2011 per Data Center Knowledge; 7.2 MW for the later expansion per Area Development, May 1, 2015, https://www.areadevelopment.com/newsitems/5-1-2015/yahoo-customer-care-center-lockport-new-york678934.shtml, seen in a search excerpt only), hence special_contract. The DELIVERY utility is not named outright in any source found. NYSEG is medium confidence on two indirect grounds: the Senate release says Yahoo secured a federal 'Green IT' grant 'through New York State Electric & Gas (NYSEG)', and NYSEG is the smaller of the two mapped territories. No source found mentions Niagara Mohawk/National Grid. Phase I opened with a ribbon-cutting on September 20, 2010 (Computerworld), so our 2023 energized year (from a 2022 generator permit) is thirteen years late. Our 90.4 MW load is far above the public allocation total and is probably installed generator capacity.

site_name: Amazon Web Services Lind Road campus (81712 Lind Rd, Hermiston)
notes: Our guess (PacifiCorp) is probably wrong, and Umatilla Electric Cooperative was not among our mapped candidates. Amazon's own article (April 4, 2023) describes Umatilla Electric Cooperative as 'the electric cooperative serving AWS in Umatilla and Morrow Counties.' That is a county-wide statement, not specific to Lind Road, hence medium rather than high; no source found ties PacifiCorp or direct Bonneville service to this site. Arrangement set to special_contract because reporting (La Grande Observer, April 11, 2023, https://lagrandeobserver.com/?p=154421) says Amazon made a deal with the cooperative to choose the electricity supply for its Boardman and Hermiston data centers rather than take the cooperative's standard supply, and that its wholesale power contracts bar disclosure of volumes. Energized year not found: two searches turned up nothing on when the first Lind Road building opened, so null (our 2019 rests only on a 2018 generator permit). No public megawatt figure found. Note that City of Hermiston enterprise-zone records (campuses PDX138 and PDX245) and 2017/2019 news stories describe other Amazon campuses west and south of Hermiston, not this one.

site_name: CoreWeave at Chirisa Technology Parks, Meadowville Technology Park (1401 Meadowville Technology Pkwy, Chester)
load_basis: Capacity of the existing building after its upgrade from 6 MW to 18 MW, which was expected to finish in June 2024 (Construction Dive, April 16, 2024). Expected, not confirmed; excludes any new-build capacity delivered in 2025.
notes: Serving utility NOT established by any acceptable source: none of the articles fetched (Construction Dive, Bisnow, Richmond BizSense, Institutional Real Estate) names the power provider, and the trade-press article that might was closed to automated access. Dominion is the only mapped territory, so our guess is likely right, but it stays an unverified map inference and the field is null. Site is the landlord Chirisa's campus at 1401 Meadowville Technology Parkway, leased to CoreWeave (Richmond BizSense, Jan 5, 2026, https://richmondbizsense.com/2026/01/05/two-new-data-centers-to-rise-on-formerly-stalled-cartograf-site-in-chesterfield/). Year: the existing building was being upgraded for mid-2024 completion (expected only), so 2024 is low confidence; the building itself predates CoreWeave's tenancy. Additional capacity: a new building of 20 MW growing to 40 MW slated for late 2025 (Construction Dive); a 50 MW build-to-suit leased to CoreWeave 'expected to deliver initial capacity in 2025' (Bisnow, Dec 16, 2024, https://www.bisnow.com/news/national/data-center/coreweave-data-center-in-virginia-lands-600m-loan-127230); and an 'initial 120 megawatts' with delivery in 2025 and 2026 (Institutional Real Estate, mid-2025). These figures overlap and should not be summed. planned_full_buildout_mw of 320 = that 120 MW plus two 100 MW buildings at 1600 Digital Drive due late 2027 and mid-2028 (Richmond BizSense); the 1600 Digital Drive site is nearby but separate, so use 120 if only this address is wanted. Our 82 MW for 2025 is within the plausible range but not confirmed.

Nothing verified from an acceptable source. Portland General Electric is the only mapped territory and directory sites list it, but no utility, operator, commission or news source naming the provider for this address was found, so serving_utility is null rather than a map inference presented as fact. Digital Realty's own Portland page lists only PDX10 (3825 NW Aloclek St) and PDX12 (5870 NE Schaaf St) and does not show this address, megawatts or dates; directory sites call this building PDX11 with a 2020 build year, which would make our 2024 (from a 2023 generator permit) too late, but that is a lead, not a citation. The permit holder is 'Beaver Ventures LLC', so the building may be a single-tenant build-to-suit. Energized year and load are null.

site_name: Applied Digital Polaris Forge 1, Ellendale (leased to CoreWeave)
load_basis: Built and energized critical IT load of Building 1 as of November 24, 2025 (Phase I, 50 MW, delivered October 2025; Phase II brought it to the full 100 MW), per the owner's press release. Critical IT capacity, not metered utility load.
notes: Our guess (Dakota Valley Electric Cooperative) is wrong. MDU Resources' June 22, 2026 release states: 'Montana-Dakota Utilities currently serves Applied Digital at Polaris Forge 1, its AI Factory near Ellendale, North Dakota.' Service is under electric service agreements approved by the North Dakota Public Service Commission (first agreement, case PU-22-371, approved June 6, 2023, https://investor.mdu.com/news/news-details/2023/MDU-Resources-Subsidiary-Receives-Regulatory-Approval-to-Serve-Large-Data-Center-Electric-Load/default.aspx; later cases PU-23-322 and PU-24-332 covered a second facility and an increase), hence special_contract. Search results also point to a commission-approved service-area agreement between Montana-Dakota and Dakota Valley for this site (case PU-23-272), which would explain the map overlap; that filing is a scanned image and was not read. IMPORTANT on the year: 2025 is when the first CoreWeave building began service. The same campus's earlier 180 MW hosting facility (not CoreWeave) 'began taking electric service on March 4' 2023 under an interim agreement; use 2023 if the question is when this campus first drew load from the utility. Our 68 MW for 2025 is below the 100 MW built by late November 2025, though the full-year average would be much lower since service began in October. Full buildout of 400 MW is the capacity contracted to CoreWeave across three buildings (same release; 250 MW lease announced June 2, 2025, later expanded by 150 MW).
